label: History
value: Anne Shirley comes to Green Gables as an orphan child
unit: Anne Shirley comes to Green Gables as an orphan child sent by mistake instead of a boy, but after initial reluctance from Marilla Cuthbert, she is officially adopted into the home. Over time, Anne forms a profound bond with her neighbor Diana Barry, solemnly pledging eternal friendship. Her vivid imagination and impulsiveness frequently lead to mishaps, such as accidentally serving Diana wine instead of raspberry cordial, causing a temporary rift with Mrs. Barry that Anne later mends by saving Diana's sick little sister. Anne continuously faces humblings and hardships, including breaking her ankle during a dare on a roof and being forced to crop her hair short after mistakenly dying it green. Academically ambitious, she pursues studies under her beloved teacher, Miss Stacy, earning a place in the elite Queen's Entrance class alongside her long-standing rival, Gilbert Blythe. After excelling at Queen's Academy and winning a college scholarship, Anne's life takes a dramatic shift when Marilla's failing eyesight threatens the future of Green Gables. Choosing family over her advanced ambitions, Anne relinquishes her scholarship to remain at home as the local teacher—a position Gilbert selflessly yields to her, bringing an end to their rivalry and sealing their new friendship.

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I’ll fold them nicely tonight. They always made us do that at the asylum. Half the time, though, I’d forget, I’d be in such a hurry to get into bed nice and quiet and imagine things."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I’d do anything to oblige you. But you’ll have to tell me what to say for this once. After I get into bed I’ll imagine out a real nice prayer to say always. I believe that it will be quite interesting, now that I come to think of it."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "But I’d be ever so much gratefuller if—if you’d made just one of them with puffed sleeves. Puffed sleeves are so fashionable now. It would give me such a thrill, Marilla, just to wear a dress with puffed sleeves."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "Oh, Marilla, I’m frightened—now that it has come I’m actually frightened. What if she shouldn’t like me! It would be the most tragical disappointment of my life."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I’ll just eat one tonight, Marilla. And I can give Diana half of them, can’t I? The other half will taste twice as sweet to me if I give some to her. It’s delightful to think I have something to give her."

label: History
value: Anne was orphaned as an infant.
unit: Orphaned as an infant, Anne was raised moving between homes, taking care of children, and living in an orphan asylum before being adopted by Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert of Green Gables. Though initially taken in by mistake instead of a boy, Anne proved her worth to the Cuthberts and was allowed to stay. She quickly made a deep home for herself at Green Gables, forming a fierce friendship with Diana Barry and navigating early mishaps, such as accidentally serving Diana currant wine and accidentally flavoring a cake with anodyne liniment for the new minister's wife. Anne also developed an intense academic rivalry with her classmate Gilbert Blythe, which began after he pulled her hair and called her 'Carrots' on his first day back at school.

label: History
value: Anne blossomed into a talented student under the mentorship of Miss Stacy.
unit: Over the years, Anne blossomed into a talented student under the mentorship of her teacher, Miss Stacy, winning over difficult figures like Diana's formidable great-aunt, Aunt Josephine, and excelling in community events like a school Christmas concert where Matthew gifted her a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves. She eventually tied with Gilbert Blythe for first place on the Island on the Queen's Academy entrance examinations. While attending Queen's, Anne won the prestigious Avery scholarship. However, upon returning home to Green Gables, tragedy struck when Matthew died suddenly from the shock of a bank failure, leaving Anne and Marilla to grieve together and look toward an uncertain future.

label: Quote
value: Anne said: "Well, that is another hope gone. ‘My life is a perfect graveyard of buried hopes.’ That’s a sentence I read in a book once, and I say it over to comfort myself whenever I’m disappointed in anything."

label: Quote
value: Anne said: “Oh, what I know about myself isn’t really worth telling,” said Anne eagerly. “If you’ll only let me tell you what I imagine about myself you’ll think it ever so much more interesting.”

label: Quote
value: Anne said: “I was afraid it might be Mrs. Spencer’s place,” said Anne mournfully. “I don’t want to get there. Somehow, it will seem like the end of everything.”

label: Quote
value: Anne said: “I—I saw it this afternoon when you were away at the Aid Society,” said Anne, a little slowly. “I was passing your door when I saw it on the cushion, so I went in to look at it.”

label: Quote
value: Anne said: “I did put it back,” said Anne quickly—pertly, Marilla thought. “I don’t just remember whether I stuck it on the pincushion or laid it in the china tray. But I’m perfectly certain I put it back.”

label: History
value: Aunt Josephine is a resident of Charlottetown.
unit: Aunt Josephine, a resident of Charlottetown, was visiting Orchard Slope when Anne Shirley and Diana Barry unexpectedly leaped onto her in a spare-room bed. Though initially furious and threatening to cancel Diana's music lessons, Miss Barry was won over when Anne bravely visited her to explain the mistake and take full responsibility. Touched by Anne's sincerity, Miss Barry decided to prolong her stay in Avonlea, and the two formed a firm friendship. She later sent Anne a pair of dainty kid slippers for Christmas and eventually invited both Anne and Diana to her Charlottetown estate, Beechwood, where she hosted them for several days of Exhibition festivities and town entertainments.

label: Quote
value: Aunt Josephine said: “I’m afraid my imagination is a little rusty—it’s so long since I used it,” she said. “I dare say your claim to sympathy is just as strong as mine. It all depends on the way we look at it. Sit down here and tell me about yourself.”

label: Quote
value: Aunt Josephine said: “I’ve made up my mind to stay simply for the sake of getting better acquainted with that Anne-girl,” she said frankly. “She amuses me, and at my time of life an amusing person is a rarity.”

label: Quote
value: Aunt Josephine said: "Mercy, child, how you have grown! You’re taller than I am, I declare. And you’re ever so much better-looking than you used to be, too. But I dare say you know that without being told."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Josephine said: "Remember, you Anne-girl, when you come to town you’re to visit me and I’ll put you in my very sparest spare-room bed to sleep."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Josephine said: "Oh, I must, hey? I rather think Diana did her share of the jumping at least. Such carryings on in a respectable house!"

label: History
value: Diana Barry formed a close friendship with Anne Shirley.
unit: Diana Barry formed a close friendship with Anne Shirley in Avonlea, engaging in typical childhood games and establishing a story club together. Her mother briefly forbade Diana from playing with Anne after Anne accidentally served her currant wine instead of raspberry cordial, causing Diana to become ill. However, the friendship was restored after Anne helped save Diana's younger sister, Minnie May, when she fell gravely ill with croup. Later, Diana and Anne unwittingly jumped onto Diana's visiting great-aunt, Aunt Josephine, in a spare-room bed, though Anne managed to appease the angry woman and secure Diana's continued music lessons. Over the following years, Diana shared in various local activities with Anne, including a Christmas concert, an autumn trip to Aunt Josephine's estate in Charlottetown for the Exhibition, and local hotel performances. As their school years progressed, Diana supported Anne through her academic pursuits, bringing the news to Green Gables that Anne had tied for first place on the Island on the Queen's Academy entrance examination, and later reuniting with Anne when she returned home after earning the Avery scholarship.

label: History
value: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea
unit: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea after spending three years in Alberta with his sick father and spending the summer visiting cousins in New Brunswick. Upon returning to school, he teased Anne Shirley by calling her 'Carrots,' which led to her smashing a slate over his head and initiating a bitter, one-sided silence and fierce academic rivalry between them. Despite saving Anne from a sinking dory on the pond, Gilbert was rebuffed when he attempted to apologize and offer his friendship. The two remained rivals as they tied for first place on the Island on the Queen's Entrance examination and went on to attend Queen's Academy together, where Gilbert ultimately won the medal while Anne earned the Avery scholarship. Upon learning that Anne planned to stay at Green Gables to care for Marilla after Matthew's death, Gilbert generously gave up his accepted teaching position in Avonlea so Anne could take it. Touched by his sacrifice, Anne forgave him, and the two finally put an end to their long rivalry and became friends.

label: History
value: Josie Pye is the last of the Pye family to attend Avonlea school.
unit: Josie Pye is the last of the Pye family to attend Avonlea school, and she famously took first prize for knitted lace at the exhibition. During a party at Diana Barry's house, Josie dared Anne Shirley to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, which resulted in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. She later attended school under Miss Stacy and was among the group of local students who studied alongside Anne and Gilbert Blythe. Josie eventually left home to attend Queen's Academy in town with her Avonlea classmates to earn her teaching license. Upon completing her studies, she graduated from Queen's alongside her peers, who celebrated various academic achievements, including scholarships and medals.

label: History
value: Lynde offered guidance to the residents of Green Gables.
unit: Lynde, a neighbor in Avonlea, offered guidance and practical support to the residents of Green Gables. She gave advice to Anne after the girl's mishaps, and she later helped Matthew by sewing a stylish puffed-sleeve dress for Anne when he sought a way to buy her modern clothing. Lynde eventually acknowledged Anne's growth and character during a visit to Marilla. She was among those who celebrated Anne's academic achievements when Anne tied for first place on the entrance exams, and she later joined the community in supporting Marilla and Anne following Matthew's sudden death.

label: Quote
value: Lynde said: "I just guess she has done well, and far be it from me to be backward in saying it. You’re a credit to your friends, Anne, that’s what, and we’re all proud of you."

label: Quote
value: Lynde said: "Child, yes, I’m afraid of it. Look at his face. When you’ve seen that look as often as I have you’ll know what it means."

label: Quote
value: Lynde said: "It’s because you’re too heedless and impulsive, child, that’s what. You never stop to think—whatever comes into your head to say or do you say or do it without a moment’s reflection."

label: Quote
value: Lynde said: "You must learn to think a little, Anne, that’s what. The proverb you need to go by is ‘Look before you leap’—especially into spare-room beds."

label: Quote
value: Lynde said: “Oh, Marilla,” she said gravely. “I don’t think—we can do anything for him.”

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert grew up as a dark, homely child.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert grew up as a dark, homely child, remaining sensitive about her childhood looks for fifty years, and later inherited an amethyst brooch from her mother. As a young woman, she was already grown up when the new house at Green Gables was built, and she once quarreled with John Blythe, refusing to forgive him. Decades later, Marilla and her brother Matthew decided to adopt an orphan boy from Nova Scotia to help on their farm, but were shocked when eleven-year-old Anne Shirley arrived by mistake instead. Though initially planning to return the girl to Mrs. Spencer, Marilla felt deep pity upon hearing Anne's tragic backstory and saved her from being taken in by the cruel Mrs. Blewett, ultimately agreeing to let her stay at Green Gables. Marilla took charge of Anne's upbringing, teaching her daily chores and bedtime prayers, and eventually defended her when Mrs. Rachel Lynde insulted the girl's appearance. Over the next few years, Marilla navigated Anne's various misadventures—including an accidental dynamic where Anne mistakenly served currant wine to Diana Barry—while gradually developing a deep, maternal love for the imaginative girl. When Anne later met with misfortunes, such as accidentally dying her hair green or breaking her ankle, Marilla faithfully nursed her and realized how precious Anne had become to her. Marilla supported Anne's academic ambitions, permitting her to take advanced classes with Miss Stacy, and felt immense pride mixed with nostalgia when Anne tied for first place on the Queen's Entrance examination and left for Queen's Academy. Following Matthew's sudden death from shock over a bank failure, Marilla learned from an oculist that her own failing sight would require her to give up reading and sewing, forcing her to consider selling Green Gables.

value: Matthew grew up at Green Gables.
unit: Matthew grew up at Green Gables and lived there into adulthood, having worn a full, soft brown beard since his twenties. When he drove Anne to Green Gables for the first time, he found himself wishing to keep the young orphan girl despite a mix-up in her adoption. He strongly advocated for Anne to stay, eventually convincing his sister Marilla to let her remain and raise her properly. Over time, Matthew consistently offered Anne warmth and encouragement, quietly supporting her interests against Marilla's more skeptical views. Recognizing Anne's plain clothing, he secretly enlisted Mrs. Rachel Lynde to make Anne a stylish brown dress with puffed sleeves for Christmas. He continued to offer gentle guidance as she grew, advising her not to give up on romance when she was discouraged. When Anne tied for first place on the Queen's Academy entrance examinations, she proudly shared the joyous news with Matthew and their family. Before Anne departed for Queen's Academy, Matthew helped her make the necessary preparations for her education.

label: Personality
value: Rachel Lynde is a capable individual.
unit: A capable, managing, and hardworking individual, Rachel Lynde is known as a kind soul who never shirks her share of work. However, she is also a critical, outspoken, and meddlesome gossip who prides herself on speaking her mind without fear or favor, to the point that she would pick faults in the Angel Gabriel himself. Additionally, she is a red-hot, enthusiastic politician, dearly loves to be asked for advice, and firmly opposes higher education for women, believing it unfits them for woman's true sphere.

label: History
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde is a prominent Avonlea housekeeper
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde is a prominent Avonlea housekeeper who raised ten children and knitted sixteen cotton warp quilts. Her curiosity was piqued when she learned the Cuthberts were adopting an orphan, and she was later insulted by Anne Shirley during a visit to Green Gables, though she quickly accepted Anne's dramatic apology. Over time, Mrs. Lynde became a source of advice for Marilla Cuthbert, suggesting how to handle Anne's school troubles and attending political events with Marilla.

As a student in Avonlea, she joined Anne Shirley's story club alongside classmates like Diana Barry and Jane Andrews to help cultivate their imaginations. When Miss Stacy organized an advanced class to prepare students for the Queen's Entrance examination, Ruby became one of the pupils who joined to study for the test. She later moved to Charlottetown to attend Queen's Academy alongside her fellow Avonlea peers. During her time at Queen's, Ruby regularly visited Anne's boarding house room with other classmates, where they shared news and discussed their academic ambitions.

unit: Anne completes her school term and travels to Charlottetown for the Queen's Academy entrance examinations. unit: During a party at Diana's house, Josie Pye dares Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, resulting in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. value: Anne and her friends reenact Tennyson's Elaine on the pond.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid
unit: Anne and her friends reenact Tennyson's Elaine on the pond, but the dory leaks and begins to sink, forcing Anne to cling to a bridge pile. Gilbert Blythe rows by and rescues her, but Anne angrily refuses his offer of apology and friendship. Later, back at Green Gables, Anne reflects on learning her lesson about romance, while Matthew gently advises her not to abandon it entirely.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
unit: During a party at Diana's house, Josie Pye dares Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, resulting in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. Mr. Barry carries Anne home, where Marilla experiences a deep realization of how much she cares for the girl. Bedridden for seven weeks while her ankle heals, Anne receives many visitors and eagerly anticipates returning to school to meet her new teacher, Miss Stacy.

value: Anne and Diana walk along Birch Path.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXVI. The Story Club Is Formed
unit: Anne and Diana walk along Birch Path on Anne's thirteenth birthday, discussing growing up, school assignments, and romantic story plots. Anne proposes starting a story club to cultivate their imaginations, which eventually expands to include other classmates like Jane and Ruby. Later, Anne talks with Marilla about the story club's progress, defending their work and sharing her aspirations to be like Mrs. Allan before Marilla prompts her to finish her household chores.

label: v1 · CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid
value: Anne and her friends reenact Tennyson's Elaine on the pond.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid
unit: Anne and her friends reenact Tennyson's Elaine on the pond, but the dory leaks and begins to sink, forcing Anne to cling to a bridge pile. Gilbert Blythe rows by and rescues her, but Anne angrily refuses his offer of apology and friendship. Later, back at Green Gables, Anne reflects on learning her lesson about romance, while Matthew gently advises her not to abandon it entirely.

unit: Diana helps Anne dress for a concert performance at the White Sands Hotel, where Marilla offers her usual blunt observations before Anne leaves with Diana, Jane, and Billy. unit: After Matthew convinces Marilla to let Anne attend a Debating Club concert and spend the night at Diana's, Anne and Diana enjoy the event together. chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue
unit: While Marilla and Mrs. Lynde attend a political rally in Charlottetown, Anne and Matthew spend a quiet evening together studying and talking. Diana Barry rushes in to beg for help because her sister Minnie May is gravely ill with croup while their parents are away. Anne hurries to the Barry home and successfully treats Minnie May using her past experience with Mrs. Hammond's children, saving the baby's life. Touched by Anne's rescue, Mrs. Barry forgives her for the past incident with Diana, allowing the two girls to be best friends once again.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid
unit: Anne and her friends reenact Tennyson's Elaine on the pond, but the dory leaks and begins to sink, forcing Anne to cling to a bridge pile. Gilbert Blythe rows by and rescues her, but Anne angrily refuses his offer of apology and friendship. Later, back at Green Gables, Anne reflects on learning her lesson about romance, while Matthew gently advises her not to abandon it entirely.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession
unit: After Matthew convinces Marilla to let Anne attend a Debating Club concert and spend the night at Diana's, Anne and Diana enjoy the event together. Upon returning home, they leap into the spare-room bed as a game, unwittingly jumping directly onto Diana's visiting great-aunt, Aunt Josephine. The resulting uproar leaves Miss Barry furious and threatens Diana's music lessons, prompting a remorseful Anne to seek a way to make amends.

unit: Anne adjusts to life at Queen's Academy, forming close friendships with Stella and Priscilla while continuing her intense academic rivalry with Gilbert. Later, Mrs. Lynde informs them that Gilbert Blythe gave up the Avonlea teaching position so Anne could have it, leading Anne to reconcile with Gilbert and look forward to her future with peace and hope.
